target: Let E be a real normed space with arbitrary chosen norm and let e:E to R^d be an algebraic linear equivalence, not assumed isometric. Let f:E to EReal be proper (no bottom anywhere, a real finite value somewhere), V a convex subset of its effective domain, and lambda>=0. Assume the exact Definition4.1 strong interpolation inequality on V in the original E norm. For p,q in V and any supplied global source subgradient vector g of u maps to f(e inverse u) at e(p), f(p)+<g,e(q-p)>+(lambda/2)||q-p||_E^2<=f(q). Values at p and q are finite by properness and domain inclusion. Zero lambda and zero g are permitted. This is the generalized forward implication of Lemma4.2 for one supplied global vector support at p, not the full iff. The printed full lemma assumes V subset dom(partial f); existence of support at every V point is neither assumed nor produced here. Coordinates supply the Euclidean pairing only; e is algebraic and the penalty uses the original E norm. No isometry, minimizer, continuity, or extra finite-dimensionality premise is added.
